items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: I stayed with Sidney band. ... we all were working with Sidney. ... I was playing still playing banjo ... with Black Sidney band.

ctx.x: Yeah. So, when we got, we made the record, I was down there at the old Italian Hall on Espinay. And they had, what they call a master disc, about this big. The electric, I think, had just about come out then, you know. And the hardest thing we had was getting the drums, not to be too loud, and the album morgan on the bass. And when we got down there, that's when I met Sidney Arden. I had been seeing him around, and I heard him play, and that guy's a terrific player. He could play just like, there was very few…
You had the tippies, where did that come from?

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: I remember guys like Frederica Ford and Beans and his white people used to come up there.

ctx.x: Well, they didn't, yeah, that's Astor Strutton.

So, Lee Collins got into thinking about the record man in town. So, he said, man, I got a record date. He said, man, I want some original tune. He said, man, the man that come up and heard, he said, we didn't know he was here, but he was back there. And I said, at that time, white people used to come to the Astor and they had a terrific flow show up there. So, Sherman Cook was the master of show em on it, they had two fellas who used to dance, they were good. And they had a little short dog woman who had a very…
Did anybody play clarinet with you regularly? No, that fella playing the clarinet.
